source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Transient global amnesia, a distinct clinical syndrome that still requires evaluation to rule out other causes such as stroke or seizure","B":"A normal, aging-related memory change generally considered to occur from time to time in most healthy older adults","C":"A fairly ordinary, expected finding in this particular situation that would not typically call for any further clinical evaluation","D":"A definitive diagnosis of stroke that can confidently be made with certainty based on this presentation alone, without further testing"}}
source_row.rationale: Transient global amnesia is a distinct clinical syndrome characterized by a sudden episode of significant memory impairment lasting hours, with otherwise preserved neurological function, and gradual resolution; despite its generally benign prognosis, it still requires evaluation to rule out other causes.
source_row.source_detail: Recognition and Evaluation of Transient Global Amnesia
source_row.source_name: American Academy of Neurology — Transient Global Amnesia
